title: Chip, Chip, Hooray: Google Eyes a $12.2 Billion Slice of Marvell
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Marvell Technology has struck a sweeping custom chip agreement with Google that could allow the technology giant to become one of the semiconductor company’s largest shareholders.

Under the arrangement, Marvell granted Google a warrant to buy as many as 58.97 million shares at $206.58 each. If exercised in full, the purchase would be worth about $12.2 billion. Most of the warrant will vest only if Google meets agreed purchasing targets through Marvell’s fiscal 2033, tying Google’s potential ownership directly to the volume of business it directs to the chipmaker.

The partnership covers a broad portfolio of custom silicon and related technologies designed to support Google’s tensor processing unit ecosystem. The companies are expected to work on components including AI accelerators, storage controllers, networking chips, memory interface controllers and near-memory computing technology.

Google’s TPUs are central to its artificial intelligence infrastructure, helping train models and run inference, the process of generating responses from trained systems. Demand for such purpose-built chips has accelerated as cloud providers seek lower costs, greater efficiency and alternatives to Nvidia’s widely used graphics processors.

The agreement also strengthens Marvell’s position against larger rival Broadcom, historically a key partner in Google’s custom chip program. Broadcom has a separate long-term agreement to develop and supply future generations of Google AI chips and components through 2031, suggesting Google is diversifying its supplier base rather than relying on a single partner.

Investors welcomed the announcement. Marvell shares jumped more than 11% in premarket trading, while Broadcom fell over 2%.

The deal arrives as major technology companies sharply increase AI spending. Combined infrastructure outlays are expected to exceed $700 billion this year, up from about $400 billion last year, intensifying competition among chip designers for lucrative custom-silicon contracts. For Marvell, the pact offers long-term revenue visibility and access to Google’s expanding infrastructure.

Source: Reuters.
